controlReview.checks: Imported GLB control-point movement tested at positive and negative commands; all 20 aircraft pass. Cockpit pairs and all ten airplane exterior pairs visually inspected. Roll, pitch, rudder and declared pedal directions corrected; ailerons and full flap deployment corrected.
limitations: Checks cover existing bindings; Cherokee and Caravan pedal geometry is static.
Full control travel and flight response remain approximations unless independently dimensioned in the model reference notes.
This audit verifies movement; it does not upgrade legacy helicopter avionics or remove previously documented geometry limitations.

cockpitReview.method: Rays from the pilotEye through source.glb (cockpit-sweep), seat view at the runtime camera (+Z, 60 degrees vertical), an exterior nose render, and sections through the pilot plane and at hood height, each checked against a photograph of the real aircraft.
findings: The panel carried a 2.0 m cabin-fit width with no absolute basis, so its 3.125 in flight dials drew at 115 mm. Its 0.28 m deep box ran through the windscreen and the corner panes, which is the black hood seen from outside.
The eye stood 1.00 m over the cushion. The floor lay on the belly, 0.13 m low, and poked through the skin chamfer; together these were the 11.3 percent of cockpit vertices reading outside the shell.
The wipers stood 0.18 m ahead of the glass at their pivot, reading as rods coming out of the hood. The pitot rods on the nose are real: the Penerbad photograph shows them.
A 0.12 m slot in the belly and a sliver between the windscreen edge and the corner pane were open to the sky.
corrections: Panel rescaled from the 3.125 in dial, hood top lowered 0.11 m and its depth cut to 0.18 m; layout and bindings unchanged.
Floor raised 0.13 m and narrowed inside the skin. Crew seats raised 0.2 m and cabin seats 0.1 m; cyclic, collective, pedals and pedestal follow.
Wipers placed on the pane; belly slot and windscreen post closed.
